description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='2023-02-29' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. No EXEC PGM= anywhere names this program - it is CALLed four times from two online programs, CORPT00C L392 and L412 and COTRN02C L393 and L413 - so it is a SERVICE and there is no PARM to declare. It opens no file either: the 157 lines carry no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, no SELECT and no FD, only WORKING-STORAGE (L22) and LINKAGE (L83), so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and leaves no final state. Its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE, here 3. Arm 3 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149, whose WHEN OTHER stays last: FC-BAD-DATE-VALUE is matched at L133 and moves 'Datevalue error' at L134, a literal that already fills WS-RESULT PIC X(15) exactly, so no padding is added and one space separates it from TstDate:. Severity and message number are DECODED from that arm's own 88-level VALUE X'000309CC59C3C5C5' (L64) rather than interpolated from a neighbour - the first halfword X'0003' is the severity, the second X'09CC' is 2508, and FACILITY-ID X'C3C5C5' is 'CEE' in EBCDIC - because the nine feedback numbers are non-contiguous (2507, 2508, 2509, 2513, 2517, 2518, 2520, 2521, skipping 2510-2512, 2514-2516 and 2519) and no one of them can be derived from another. The date reaches this arm because 2023 is not divisible by four, which makes February 28 days long by the Gregorian rule rather than by any runtime calendar call, so day 29 overflows the month. Each component is separately legitimate, which is what isolates 2508: the text is fully numeric where the mask wants digits, so this is not FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA 2520 (case18, case19); 02 is a real month, so it is not FC-INVALID-MONTH 2517 (case12 to case14); and 2023 is far inside the supported range, so it is not FC-UNSUPP-RANGE 2513 (case10, case11). Only the combination is impossible. case08 reaches the same arm from the other side of the month-length lookup, 31 June in a 30-day month, so the two together drive both branches. The echoed date is deliberately WRONG and must stay so: the group move at L122 overwrites the clean copy planted at L107-L108 with WS-DATE-TO-TEST, whose leading two bytes are Vstring-length PIC S9(4) BINARY (L26) holding LENGTH OF LS-DATE, the declared width 10 = X'000A' (L105), so WS-DATE PIC X(10) keeps only those two binary bytes plus the first eight characters. The '29' that makes the date invalid is therefore discarded, and the message names the error without ever showing the offending value - preserved as legacy behaviour, not repaired. WS-DATE-FMT (L55) is filled at L111-L113 before the CALL and is not a target of L122, so it stays clean. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57, the token at L64, the arm at L133-L134 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run: no Language Environment CEE* service exists here, so CEEDAYS cannot be executed and the validator is hand-written.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '2023-02-29' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
